turns.text: Dust coats the tongue before the eyes bother opening — concrete dust, rebar-rust dust, the specific stale grit of a wall that used to stand somewhere it doesn't anymore. Vent housing holds warm around the shoulders, the only thing round here that still remembers its shape. Paws haven't decided to move. The dust already has an opinion about tonight.

the rubble field stretches flat and broken where a tower of flats used to stack twelve stories of noise, and over the flattest stretch of it a holo-grid flickers up a parking lot that was never poured — clean white lines, phantom sedans blinking into place one row at a time, tires that never touch actual ground. a survey drone threads low between the projected cars, its scanner painting the debris in soft blue grid-light, logging drift a centimeter at a time, patient as rot.

Ears track the drone's scan-hum without the rest of the body agreeing to care yet — old sound, filed under harmless a long time ago, back when there was still a wall here to file things behind. Rises anyway. Stalks the vent's mouth toward the rubble's edge, low, unhurried, weight testing each broken slab before trusting it.

the slabs hold, mostly — rebar poking through at odd angles, some bent to hooks by the old demolition claw, none of it sharp enough yet to have drawn blood from anything that knows where to step. a phantom sedan renders directly overhead, translucent, its holo-shadow passing through solid concrete without either one noticing the other. underfoot, the real ground remembers being a building far more precisely than the projection does.

A drone housing lies half-buried near the rubble's edge, cracked open on its own, rotor bent stiff and useless — not this cat's doing, not tonight's, but familiar enough to bite anyway. Teeth close on the casing's ragged seam out of something closer to habit than hunger. It doesn't taste like anything. Bites again regardless.

the casing gives a little more under the second bite, wiring inside sparking one weak, dying blue before going dark for good. a plaque half-buried near the housing reads NEKOCORP DEMOLITION SERVICES — SECTOR CLEARANCE COMPLETE, the date on it three years gone. the holo-grid stutters as a phantom car clips the real wreckage wrong, and for one full second the projection glitches through — not a parking lot, but the building that stood here, windows lit warm, laundry strung between two balconies, gone again before the eye finishes arriving.

Freezes mid-bite, jaw still locked on dead wire. Whatever that flicker was, it doesn't smell like anything, doesn't sound like anything, shouldn't matter — and matters anyway, the way an old wound matters when weather changes. Doesn't look back at where it was. Spits the wire out. Keeps walking.

the grid smooths back over to clean white lines and patient phantom traffic, the glitch already filed under scheduled maintenance somewhere a satellite up never sleeps. past the plaque, a chunk of standing wall still holds — spray-scrawled across it, half-legible under newer tags, a warning some other cat left about a block over: spiders don't leave the wire, something something research basement, don't lick the panels. the paint's gone ozone-sharp at the edges, a smell that doesn't fully wash out no matter how much rain gets at it.

Nose brushes the scrawl once, files the warning the way any secondhand rumor gets filed — somebody else's block, somebody else's trouble, worth remembering exactly as long as it takes to forget on purpose. Doesn't linger on the ozone smell either. Moves past it toward the rubble's far edge, where the drone's scan-hum has thinned to almost nothing.

the far edge drops into a service trench, half-filled with runoff gone milky from concrete dust, a length of chain-link folded flat where something heavier than a cat pushed through it recently. overhead, drone-band chatter crackles thin through the survey unit's idle speaker — routine sign-off, sector clear, structural drift within tolerance — before it banks off toward the next flattened block on its list.

Drops flat at the trench's lip anyway, out of a habit older than tonight's reason for it, watching the drone bank away without needing to know why watching matters. The milky runoff smells like nothing worth drinking. Waits until the rotor-hum folds back into the rubble field's general quiet before trusting the legs to move again.

the field settles back to its usual layered quiet — holo-traffic looping clean and empty, the plaque's three-year-old date unchanged, the ozone-tagged wall keeping its secondhand warning for whoever reads it next. somewhere past the chain-link, a NekoCorp billboard two blocks over cycles a jingle too far off to catch words, just a shape of brightness bleeding upward into low cloud.

Turns back toward the vent without deciding to, the way a body just knows which direction is warm. Passes the bent-rotor housing again on the way, gives it one last idle bite out of nothing but consistency. Still doesn't taste like anything. Still worth doing.

the vent's mouth breathes its familiar leftover warmth up through broken ductwork, same as it did an hour ago, same as it'll do tomorrow. the holo-grid keeps rendering its clean white lines over ground that remembers better than any projection does. nothing here gets rebuilt so much as pretended over, and the pretending runs on a schedule nobody down here was asked about.

Circles twice inside the vent's mouth, dust settling back out of the fur in a fine gray sift. The flicker from earlier — warm windows, strung laundry — doesn't come back, and doesn't get chased after either. Some things stay buried on purpose. Eyes go to slits, then further, dust still faintly bitter behind the teeth.

the rubble field holds its quiet through the last dark hour, phantom cars parking themselves into rows nobody will ever walk between, the survey drone's log ticking one more clean entry onto a list that never shortens. the ozone-tagged wall keeps its warning. the plaque keeps its date. everything down here waits without knowing it's waiting, which is its own kind of rest.
